summary: Took five repo residue charts I(1,2), I(2,2), I(1,5), II(1,5), I(2,3) (s<=6) on the 39,174 primes = 1 mod 4 up to 1e6 and computed all pairwise/triple/quadruple intersections. The nerve is degenerate, not CRT-independent: I(1,2)=I(2,2) exactly (also =II(1,2)), II(1,5) is a subset of I(1,5), I(1,2) and I(2,3) are disjoint, and no prime lies in all five (core 0; 4,817 primes in none); every pairwise observed/independent ratio is 0, 1 or 2 (disjoint, independent-looking, or nested/equal). Across all 395 charts with s<=60 only 146 distinct covered sets remain on primes up to 1.2e6 (Z1122).
not_done: Charts are taken as the repo's residue claims (leastfam/dividing formulas); I did not re-verify each certificate formula. Five charts were chosen by hand from s<=6, not by an optimisation.
next: Deduplicate the chart atlas by covered set (146 distinct for s<=60) before any chart-count claim.

summary: Premise check: the cleared equation 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) has degree 1 in each variable (sympy), so for fixed (n,y,z) the x-root is unique and no Vieta/Markoff jump exists (0 non-trivial R2 moves over 50,602 solutions with n<=300). Rule R1 (gcd-descent n->n/g, valid by homogeneity) applies to 22,195 solutions and decreases n, max denominator and sum in every case. For prime n no R1 move exists (g=n would need 4 = sum of three unit fractions), so the only well-founded step is vacuous for ES instances with prime n.
not_done: Did not search for other rewrite rules (e.g., from other forms of the equation); R3 (sorting) is only noted as measure-neutral.
next: Drop Vieta/Markoff rewriting for the 3-term equation; any termination claim must use a different (non-linear) reformulation.

summary: Jobs = 146 distinct repo charts (s<=60) with cost proxy s; schedules evaluated on held-out primes 1 mod 4 in (1e6,1.2e6] (7,254 primes) with training on (1e5,5e5]. Mean cost per prime: least-cost-first 113, round-robin 775, residue-conditioned (order by train success/cost per class mod 840) 63, oracle 55; 69 primes are uncovered by any chart under every schedule. Residue-conditioning is nearly oracle, but coverage is itself a residue-class function, so this is engineering, not new mathematics.
not_done: Cost is the proxy s, not measured wall time; the family cost table is not calibrated against actual runs. Round-robin is the cyclic rotation of the cost order, one of several possible definitions.
next: If a portfolio is ever built, use the residue-conditioned order with measured costs.

summary: Game (A picks 1/x, B picks 1/y, A picks 1/z, A wins iff the residual is exactly 0): for every prime p = 1 mod 4 <= 3000 (211 primes) and every tested first move x (window 2000) B has a refuting reply (0 A-surviving moves). Proof (PROVED): with 4/p - 1/x = a/b reduced and k = floor((b+1)/a)+1, the reply y = kb leaves residual (ka-1)/(kb) whose reduced numerator exceeds 1, so A can never finish; checked on 422,000 (p,x) pairs. The premise 'winning positions = positive three-term decompositions' is false: A must survive every reply (exists x forall y exists z), which fails at every first move.
not_done: The game with a different turn structure or bounded denominators was not analysed.
next: Replace the game by the plain existential ES search; the EXISTS-FORALL version is trivially lost by the second player.

summary: Exact solution sets S (ordered x<=y<=z, no box truncation) for p in {5..97} define a loopy factor graph on X,Y,Z. With the full 3-ary exact factor plus ordering factors, sum-product BP reproduces the exact marginals (mean L1 error < 5e-5), but that is trivially so because the factor is the whole support. The pairwise-projection triangle (the loopy relaxation) has mean L1 error 0.14 (p=13), 0.41 (p=29), 0.58 (p=61), 0.71 (p=89), 1.00 (p=97, not converged in 500 iterations).
not_done: Only p<=97 (exact enumeration). Did not build a residue-factor (modular) factor graph; the variables are the denominators themselves.
next: Keep the 3-ary exact factor; pairwise cavity messages carry no usable marginals for ES.

summary: Energy on the box x,y in [ceil(p/4), +2p) for p<=97: E = distance to divisibility of pxy by D = 4xy-p(x+y) (E=0 iff a certificate), with a large penalty for D<=0. Each box has 4-12 zero-energy points but 68-3694 strict local minima with E>0; steepest descent from all grid points ends at a zero point from 9.2% (p=13) down to 0.6% (p=97) of starts. The landscape is rugged and the zero basin shrinks with p.
not_done: Only unit-coordinate moves on (x,y), no z-coordinate moves; no simulated annealing or other search dynamics were tried.
next: Do not use the divisibility energy as a search heuristic; the basin statistics already show it is uninformative.

summary: Success bias b(a) on the 96 classes of H = {a in (Z/840)^*: a = 1 mod 4} (fraction of primes 1 mod 4 <= 1e6 covered by repo charts with s<=60). The convolution operator on H is diagonalised by its 96 characters; the only non-trivial deficit lies on {1,121,169,289,361,529} (b = 0.81-0.84), which is exactly the square subgroup H^2, so 99.8% of the non-trivial Fourier energy sits on the 15 order-2 characters (the characters trivial on H^2). No new outlier beyond the known square-class structure (BRAINSTORM/y5_ocensus_hard_primes.md:29 states these classes are quadratic residues mod 840).
not_done: Used m=840 (not 4C); the 'operator' is the Cayley convolution by the bias itself, so its spectrum is the Fourier transform of the bias, not an independent transition operator.
next: None needed: the spectral view only restates the square-class description of the hard primes.

summary: Built an exact QUBO for bounded 4/n search: F = (4xyz - n(xy+yz+zx))^2 over B-bit x,y,z, multilinearised and Rosenberg-reduced with product ancillas (not adder carries). For n=3, B=3 (54 variables, 45 ancillas) and n=3, B=4 (130 variables) the zero-energy set equals the brute-force box solutions; n=5 and n=2 also match. Gadget exactness, E(forced ancillas)=F for all inputs, and single-ancilla flips (no decrease) were checked exhaustively over inputs.
not_done: Full ground-state enumeration over all variables is infeasible (2^54 and up); exactness for non-forced ancilla values rests on the Rosenberg penalty weight M, verified only locally. Carries of an adder-based encoding were not implemented.
next: The encoder is reusable; a QUBO solver run would not add ES content at this scale.

summary: Network of k<=10 distinct repo charts with variables v_i = p mod m_i, unary chart tensors and pairwise CRT tensors [v_i = v_j mod gcd(m_i,m_j)]. Every pair interacts (all m_i divisible by 4), so the interaction graph is complete: exact treewidth = k-1 (subset DP), and the exact minimum weighted elimination cost equals the naive product of domains (k=10: 7.2e13) with no contraction saving; random orders are no better.
not_done: Did not use the actual pairwise chart tensors' structure beyond their support pattern (contraction cost was computed from domain sizes only).
next: Residue-selection networks of this form offer no contraction advantage; skip further width work.

summary: Congruence basis changes C -> T^T C T: for the 16 Boolean binary tensors (104 GL2(Z) transforms with entries <=2) 7 become sparser; for Z/8 tensors C_g = [a = b mod g] the random unimodular search gives C_1 64->4, C_2 32->8, C_4 16->7, while C_8 (identity; the chart-pair constraint I(1,2)/I(2,2)) stays at 8. PROVED: the congruence orbit of a positive definite symmetric matrix has every row with a positive diagonal entry, so nnz >= n and identity-type constraints cannot be sparsified.
not_done: Random search only for Z/8 (not exhaustive); only congruence (T^T C T) transforms, not general holographic bases over C (Fourier) or multi-edge bases.
next: None for ES: the fine equality constraints are basis-invariant in sparsity.

summary: The cleared equation is homogeneous of degree 3 in (n,x,y,z), so solutions are points of a surface in P^3 and the balanced height is the product-formula sum, equal to the archimedean log max of the primitive representative. Over all 433 solutions with p=1 mod 4 <= 297 (29 primes): S3 permutations change the height by 0, and every solution is primitive (gcd(p,x,y,z)=1, since g=p would force 4 = sum of three unit fractions), so the rescaling transformation is vacuous for prime n.
not_done: Did not define a non-trivial p-adic weight (the product formula kills it on primitive points). The second transformation was checked only on primitive representatives, so it is trivially unchanged.
next: A height descent for prime-n ES instances needs a different transformation than gcd rescaling.

summary: McCormick envelope (upper bounds w<=U1, w<=U2 on w=xy) on boxes in x in [ceil(p/4)+1, floor(3p/4)], y>=x, with exact box-maximisation of 4 min(U1,U2) - p(x+y) (vertices and line-edge intersections) to prune boxes where D = 4xy-p(x+y) >= 1 is impossible. Pruned only 17% (p=13) to 6.4% (p=97) of integer points; no true solution was ever pruned (soundness), and the surviving leaves are almost all non-solutions because the envelope is blind to divisibility.
not_done: Only the positivity constraint is relaxed; the divisibility D | pxy and the z-integrality are not in the relaxation. No LP solver was used (exact vertex enumeration instead).
next: A convex relaxation of ES must encode divisibility, which McCormick cannot do; skip further envelope work.

summary: Additive DFT on Z/840 of three distributions over primes <= 2e4 (p=1 mod 4, 1,124 primes): all primes (|supp| 96, |supp hat| 840), uncovered primes (|supp| 2, 3 primes only), and the divisor-residue distribution of the repo charts (|supp| 145, |supp hat| 840). Products 80,640 / 1,680 / 121,800 are all >= 840 as Donoho-Stark requires, and 300 random sub-collections of divisor distributions have minimum product 1,660.
not_done: The uncovered-prime sample (3 primes) is far too small to see the six square classes; the divisor distribution is my reading of the item (f | N_c over charts), not a canonical object. Only the additive group was used.
next: Use the Donoho-Stark bound as a sanity check only; it carries no ES content.

summary: SAT encoding of x,y,z in [1,1023] (10 bits each) with 4xyz = 13(xy+yz+zx): shift-add multipliers and ripple-carry adders as explicit Tseitin circuits (13,417 variables, 45,096 clauses), enumerated by minisat with blocking clauses (4 min 17 s on one core). It returns 24 models, equal to the 24 ordered permutations of the four sorted solutions (4,18,468), (4,20,130), (4,26,52), (5,10,130), and every decoded model is verified exactly in integers.
not_done: Only p=13 and B=10 (larger B or other p not run). The blocking-clause loop re-solves from scratch each time.
next: The encoding is validated; scaling to larger p is a compute question, not a finding.
